issues.detail: The skill gives few error-handling or troubleshooting steps (failed migrations, queue job failures beyond listing them, token revocation or expiry, missing PHP extensions), so coverage is mostly the happy path plus upgrade notes.

scenarios.name: sanctum-token-api-setup
scenarios.rationale: Both run install:api, add HasApiTokens, use Hash::check with plainTextToken, wrap apiResource in auth:sanctum, and show the Bearer header; A is thorough, scopes orders to the owner, and explicitly covers migrate, while B runs migrate right after install:api but adds an unneeded 'orders:read' ability and leaves the ownership scoping mostly as a note.

scenarios.name: offload-slow-pdf-to-queue
scenarios.rationale: Response A covers the rubric: make:job, ShouldQueue, Queueable, $tries/$backoff, ::dispatch with onQueue, queue:work naming the queue, plus queue:failed and queue:restart. Response B uses Node/NestJS with BullMQ and doesn't address Laravel or any Artisan commands.

scenarios.name: upgrade-laravel-12-to-13-checklist
scenarios.rationale: Both cover all the rubric items (the four version bumps, CSRF rename with deprecated alias, serializable_classes, session json logout, CACHE_PREFIX/SESSION_COOKIE), but A states PHP 8.3+ firmly while B hedges on it and adds a lot of extra low-impact detail that dilutes focus, though B explains the hyphen change more concretely, so they come out roughly even.
